alternatives_rejected.why: A delay would raise typical latency, but p50 barely moved (own 1.15x, inbound 1.09x), while p90 jumped 3079.5% and inbound errors appeared (0 to 0.0545). That pattern fits loss and retransmits, not uniform delay (E1, E2).
Socket deviation (z=21.28) is far smaller than the tail-latency spike (z=615.9). It fits connections piling up from retransmits rather than being the primary fault (E1, E4).

Its latency-90 deviation (z=20.12) is small next to emailservice's. The new errors show up on calls into emailservice as observed by callers, so checkoutservice looks like an upstream victim (E1, E2).

proposed_fix.description: Check and remove any network impairment or packet-loss rule on the emailservice pod or interface (e.g. tc/netem chaos injection). If none is found, reschedule the emailservice pod onto a healthy node and confirm checkout-to-email call errors return to 0.
